title: A kinematical investigation of the bipolar planetary nebula NGC 650-1

evidence.locator: Read as the page scans the Astrophysics Data System serves (A&A 307, pp. 253 to 270). Abstract: "a bipolar wind-driven bubble orientated at an inclination of ~ 75° with the NW lobe pointing towards the observer"; a bright central ring with two attached inner lobes, typical expansion velocities about 43 and 60 km/s; fainter outer lobes at about 5 km/s; a polar cap on the south-east side. Sect. 1 (p. 255): the rectangular bright core is about 95 by 42 arcsec at position angle about 35°; the inner lobes extend about 85 arcsec from the central star, the outer ones up to about 135 arcsec (north-west) and 165 arcsec (south-east); the isophotal major axis of the whole nebula is at position angle −55°; a distance of 1.2 kpc (Felli & Perinotto 1979). Sect. 4.1 (pp. 260 to 262): the ring's diameter, 93 arcsec, from the rectangle's major axis; its two sides along the central slit are 22.5 arcsec (blue) and 33 arcsec (red) long, 50 arcsec together with an overlap of 5.5; each end of the ring projects as an ellipse with minor axes 17 and 27 arcsec; an inclination of 73° to 80°; the two components are 85.5 km/s apart at the centre, about 43 km/s along the sight line, and with 76° adopted the expansion velocity is about 44 km/s; a systemic velocity of −25 ± 1 km/s; the approaching side of the ring is toward the south-east, the north-west lobe extends towards the observer and the south-east lobe away; the inner lobes' two components are up to 120 km/s apart along the sight line. Fig. 7: the thick ring seen 15° from edge-on. Fig. 11: a side-view sketch of the ring, the inner lobes and the outer lobes.
